questions.q_en: Find the single discount equivalent to a series discount of 30%, 20% and 15%

Let the marked price = Rs 100

= Rs 47.6

Therefore, required discount = 100 - 47.6

= 52.4 %

questions.q_en: A shopkeeper sold similar article to his two customers A and B. To customer A he allows, two successive discounts of 10% and 20% respectively while to customer B he allows, two successive discounts of 15% each. The difference between the selling price of article B to A is Rs.4. If the marked up per cent of the article is 60% above its cost price, then what is the profit amount earned by shopkeeper when he sold the article to customer B?
questions.solution_en:
Let the marked price of the article = 100x

Selling price of article to customer A after two successive discounts = 90% of 80% of 100x = 72x

Selling price of article to customer B after two successive discounts = 85% of 85% of 100x = 72.25x

According to question-

72.25x - 72x = 4

0.25x = 4

x = 16

Selling price of article to customer B after two successive discounts = 72.25x = Rs.1156

Marked price of article = 100x = Rs.1600

Cost price of article = 1600 * (100/160) = Rs.1000

Profit amount when the article is sold to B = 1156 - 1000 = Rs.156

questions.q_en: Kiran sold a copper jug to Sohil at 21% profit and Sohil sold it to Zinat at (100/11)% of profit and Zinat again sold it to Varsha at (100/3)% of profit. If Varsha purchased the copper jug at Rs. 2970, then at what price Kiran purchased the copper jug.
questions.solution_en:
Let the cost price of copper jug for Kiran = Rs. 100x

Cost price of copper jug for Sohil = Rs. 100x * 121/100 = Rs. 121x

Cost price of copper jug for Zinat = Rs. 121x * 12/11 = Rs. 132x

Cost price of copper jug for Varsha = Rs. 132x * 4/3 = Rs. 176x

=> 2970 = 176x

=> x = 2970/176 = 16.875

So, Kiran purchased the copper jug = Rs. 100 * 16.875 = Rs. 1687.5

questions.q_en: Profit percentage earned after selling an article for Rs. 2425 is equal to the loss percentage incurred after selling the article for Rs. 1455. Find cost price of the article.
questions.solution_en:
Let the cost price of the article = Rs. X

According to question,

(2425 - X)/X * 100 = (X - 1455)/X * 100

2425 - X = X - 1455

2X = 3880

X = Rs. 1940

questions.q_en: Shikha sold a handbag at the price 11% above the cost price. If she had bought it at 8% less than what she actually paid for it and sold it at the price which is Rs. y more than the actual selling price, then she would have gained 25%. Find the ratio of value of y to the original cost price of the handbag.
questions.solution_en:
Let cost price of handbag = Rs. 100

In first condition,

Selling price of handbag = 100* (100 + 11)/100 = Rs.111

In second condition,

New cost price of handbag = 100* (100 - 8)/100 = Rs.92

New selling price of handbag = 92* (100 + 25)/100 = 92* 5/4 = Rs.115

ATQ,

y = 115 - 111

y = 4

Required ratio = 4: 100 = 1: 25

questions.q_en: Raghav sold a T-shirt at 10% profit. Had he purchased the t-shirt at 10% less price and sold the t-shirt at Rs. 160 less, then he would have earned 16(2/3)% profit. What would have been the selling price of the t-shirt had he sold it at 20% profit?
questions.solution_en:
Let CP = Rs. 100x

SP = Rs. 110x

New CP = Rs. 90x

And New SP = (110x - 160)

Profit % = 16(2/3)%

(110x - 160 - 90x)/90x * 100 = 16(2/3)%

=> x = 32

So, selling price of the t-shirt if he sold it at 20% of profit = 3200 * 120/100 = Rs. 3840

questions.q_en: A shopkeeper sells 250kg of sugar. He sells 'y' kg quantity of sugar at 14% loss and the remaining quantity at 24% loss. He loses 20% on total quantity. Find the value of 'y'.
Some pens are bought at 12 for Rs 100 and an equal number of pens at 18 for Rs 130. If all the pens are sold at Rs 120 per dozen then find the profit percentage (%).
questions.solution_en:
Given - pen at 12 for Rs 100 = pen at 18 for Rs 130

Let total pen (LCM of 12 & 18) = 36

Let 36 pens are bought at 12 for Rs 100

Then cost of 36 pens = 100 X 36/12 = 300 Rs

Let 36 pens are bought at 18 for Rs 130

Then cost of 36 pens = 130 X 36/18 = 260 Rs

Total cost of 72 pens = 300 + 260 = 560 Rs

SP of 12 pens = 120

SP of 1 pen = 120/12 = 10 Rs.

SP of 72 pens = 10 X 72 = 720 Rs.

Profit percent = profit X 100/CP

= (720 - 560) X 100 / 560

= 160 X 100 / 560

= 200/7

questions.q_en: A shopkeeper offers a discount of 7% on the marked price of an almirah and still makes a profit of 24%. If he gains Rs. 21600 on the sale of the almirah, then what is the marked price of the almirah?
questions.solution_en:
Let the CP of the almirah be 100x.

SP of the almirah = 100x * (124/100) = 124x

MP of the almirah = 124x * (100/93) = 400x/3

Profit = 124x - 100x = 24x

=> 24x = 21600

=> x = 21600 /24 = 900

MP of the almirah = 400/3 * 900 = Rs. 120000
